Title: TVS voltage protection for 15A automotive circuit

I'm making a PCB for a glorified switch which has the car battery as its input and two 50W outputs which each can be switched on and off via the VN7003ALH ST-Microelectronics' high side switch, it is made for automotive applications and can handle high voltages and currents.

I need to protect all the circuit from transient voltages, load dumps, etc.
 The input powers:

- the two VN7003ALH
- 5V buck regulator which powers an IC which is used to control everything
- another logical signal that shouldn't need much current (but is still directly taken after the schottky, and it will have a fuse, although I don't know which)
- a voltage divider used to sense the battery voltage (15k and 7.5k, should provide 5V when having 15V, there's a zener diode to avoid overvoltage on the MCU pin)

since it needs to hold 15A of continuous current I can't insert a regulator between the fuse and the load, so I though I needed to use a TVS which also helps with everything else.

For now I came up with this, though I'm not really sure of it.

simulate this circuit – Schematic created using CircuitLab

I'm sure about the reverse polarity protection being after the fuse, but I don't know/understand some things:

- should the TVS be before or after the fuse? Because if it after the fuse in case of a load dump it might blow, if it is before it might try to clamp the voltage for too much time and burn out
- can I use the TVS as a "voltage regulator" to stabilize the voltage at around ~15V maximum?
- am I missing some other things?

Note: I though of adding an EMI filter, but apparently it is not needed in my case, since the radios I'll connect to the outputs will have various filters inside their power supply. Also, each power output has a 5A fuse.

EDIT: The reason why the two output combined can draw a maximum of 10A and the main fuse is 15A (the buck regulator fuse is 1A) is that I'm designing it with everything a bit "bigger" than it should be, so in any case it will hold well under stress.

Title: Where was the Mummers Parade scene in It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia filmed?

In It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia S18E02, "Dennis and Dee Don't Get Rich," Dee and Dennis find themselves in the middle of a Mummers Parade. As Charlie and Frank planned, the parade also serves as a funeral for Bonnie and Sam, whom they ended up launching from a cannon.

The background includes what appear to be Philadelphia landmarks: several buildings, the Benjamin Franklin Bridge, and the Delaware River. Given that the scene also features the Philadelphia Mummers Parade, I wonder whether the production filmed on location in Philadelphia for authenticity instead of relying on their usual Los Angeles sets.

Where was this scene shot? Was it filmed on location in Philadelphia, or did they use another place as a stand-in?

As with other film-location questions, I am looking for a specific answer (for example, the exterior of Paddy's Pub is known to be at 544 Mateo Street in Los Angeles, CA) rather than just the general city.

Title: Could an Entire People Bathe in Pomegranate Juice?

I’m working on a fantasy world that contains a place called the Rotten Corpse Lands, a vast and strange environment centered around corpses, decay, and the continuous reproduction of life from death. I’m trying to figure out how the inhabitants of this region would use one of their strangest natural resources: pomegranates.

In this world, pomegranates are not simply a food or crop. They are the main source of water in the Rotten Corpse Lands.

What are the pomegranates of the Rotten Corpse Lands?

The pomegranates here are completely different from ordinary pomegranates. They are enormous fruits, roughly the size of a large watermelon, with a deep crimson color and a huge amount of fresh, refreshing juice. The strangest part is that these fruits grow inside the corpses of creatures called Corpse Bearers, specifically within a cavity in their bodies that resembles a womb.

Corpse Bearers are the main creatures inhabiting the Rotten Corpse Lands. They include a huge variety of beings, ranging from humanoid creatures, to enormous flesh giants, to small red goblin-like creatures, as well as strange plant- and animal-like organisms. These creatures die constantly, and after death their bodies eventually become part of the environment itself. Despite this, enormous pomegranates can be found growing inside some of these corpses.

These fruits are produced in enormous quantities throughout the region, reaching hundreds of thousands, and they therefore serve as the main source of water. The inhabitants do not rely on rivers and freshwater lakes in the same way we do. Instead, most of their water comes from pomegranate juice. They drink it directly, collect and store it, use it for cooking, and use it for other everyday activities that require water.

One important aspect of the setting is that the fact that the pomegranates grow inside corpses does not necessarily mean the fruit itself is rotten or contaminated. On the contrary, the strange part of the concept is that a fresh, clean, juice-rich fruit can grow inside a dead and decaying body, as if it were part of a unique ecosystem belonging to the Rotten Corpse Lands.

How would the inhabitants use this water?

Since pomegranate juice is effectively their primary source of water, I assume the inhabitants would use it not only for drinking, but also for everyday activities in general. It could potentially be used for cooking, cleaning, bathing, caring for the body, cooling things, and other purposes that normally require water.

This leads to the main question I’d like to ask the [this site] community:

Would it make sense for the inhabitants of the Rotten Corpse Lands to bathe in pomegranate juice?

If this juice is essentially their only practical source of freshwater, would bathing in it become completely normal for them, or would there be problems that make it impractical?

For example, I’m wondering about things such as the stickiness caused by the juice, its sugar content, smell, attracting insects or other creatures, how quickly it might spoil, whether it would cling to the skin, cause irritation, or need to be diluted or processed before being used for bathing.

I’m also interested in the cultural side of this. If an entire population grew up in an environment where freshwater is extremely rare, but huge quantities of pomegranate juice are available, could bathing in pomegranate juice become a completely ordinary part of daily life, even though it would seem extremely strange to someone from outside the Rotten Corpse Lands?

I’m not only looking for a simple “yes or no” answer. I’d like ideas that could help me make this water system feel believable from an ecological, practical, and cultural worldbuilding perspective.

Title: Does this centered alternating sum involving $p_n/n$ converge?

Let $p_n$ denote the $n$-th prime. Consider

$$ C_N= \sum_{n=1}^{2N}(-1)^{n-1}\frac{p_n}{n} + \frac{p_{2N}}{4N}. $$

Numerically, $C_N$ appears to converge to a value around

$$ 1.72. $$

The correction term is natural because

$$ C_{N+1}-C_N= -\frac12 \left( \frac{p_{2N+2}}{2N+2}- 2\frac{p_{2N+1}}{2N+1} + \frac{p_{2N}}{2N} \right), $$

so the increments of $C_N$ are exactly governed by the second differences of $p_n/n$.

This is reminiscent of Pillai-type alternating sums of primes, but here each prime is weighted by $1/n$, with an endpoint correction suggested by the exact second-difference identity above.

My questions are:

- Does $C_N$ converge?
- If so, can this be proved from known results, or does it depend on deeper open questions concerning alternating prime sums or odd/even indexed prime-gap fluctuations?

Title: Best known explicit constructions of large prime gaps

X-posted from [another site]

The classical construction showing that prime gaps can be unbounded is considering the numbers $n!+2,\cdots,n!+n$, this outputs $n-1$ consecutive composite numbers, and so, prime gaps can be arbitrarily large. Letting

$$G(x)=\max_{p_n\leq x} (p_{n}-p_{n-1})$$

this proof gives a lower bound of the type

$$G(x)\gtrsim\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}.$$

This bound has been improved many times, the best known one as I'm writing this post is

$$G(x)\gtrsim\frac{\log _2^2x\log_4 x}{\log_3 x}\log x$$

where $\log_tx$ denotes the $t$-th iterated logarithm. As far as I understand, this latter bound, and the couple best known before it, were probabilistic arguments, and therefore non-explicit. My question is what's the best known explicit lower bound? The first bound given above can be beaten by taking the numbers $n\#+2,\cdots,n\#+n$ where

$$n\#=\prod_{p\leq n}p$$

this giving a lower bound of

$$G(x)\gtrsim\log x$$

at this point one may wonder what exactly qualifies as "explicit", for definiteness say, that for every $n$ one can find a number $f(n)$ in polynomial time such that $f(n),f(n)+1,\cdots,f(n)+n-1$ are all composite. Thus, the two explicit bounds I gave above are indeed explicit.

As far as I understand Rankin's proof of

$$G(x)\gtrsim\frac{\log_2 x\log_4x}{\log_3^2x}\log x$$

is via a greedy algorithm, so it should also be explicit, though saying it for certain would require one to go through a complexity analysis of their algorithm. Is this where the story ends? Since Rankin's bound was beaten has there been any work on explicit lower bounds (like it has been the case for other hard to compute functions, such as Ramsey numbers)?

Title: Statistical significance of heuristic search results on the 1939 Diagapeyev Cipher

I am investigating the historical Diagapeyev Cipher (1939), which lacks a documented decryption procedure. I have developed an open-source heuristic optimization framework to analyze the cipher's structural properties.

My approach:

Model: A 6×6 permutation matrix model.

Search Strategy: Large-scale stochastic hill-climbing guided by a Russian trigram language model.

Results: The optimization consistently converges to a high-scoring configuration (Log-score: 15.84). Statistical validation via Monte Carlo sampling (N=10,000) places this result in the extreme upper tail of the empirical null distribution (p_tail ≤ 10^-4).

My Question:
 I would appreciate insights from the community on whether the emergence of Russian linguistic fragments in this search space represents a robust cryptanalytic finding, or if it should be primarily interpreted as an artifact of the local trigram scoring model given the cipher's under-specified nature.

Title: ISO 2081 Fe/Zn12/C – Does it require an iridescent finish, or can a clear/natural finish also comply?

I'm looking for some clarification from people with experience in electroplating and engineering specifications.

The drawing specifies:

Protection zinc plating: ISO 2081 – Fe/Zn12/C

Our plating supplier delivers an iridescent zinc finish and states that it complies with ISO 2081 Fe/Zn12/C.

However, our customer rejected the appearance, re-plated the parts, and informed us that they require a natural (clear) zinc finish instead.

The drawing does not specify:

- Clear passivation
- Trivalent or hexavalent passivation
- Appearance color
- Top coat or sealer

It only specifies:

- ISO 2081 – Fe/Zn12/C

My questions are:

- Does ISO 2081 Fe/Zn12/C necessarily imply an iridescent finish?
- Can a clear/natural zinc finish also comply with this specification?
- From an engineering and quality standpoint, would you consider this drawing ambiguous, or should the desired passivation/appearance be explicitly specified?

I'm not trying to determine who is right or wrong. My goal is to understand how this specification is commonly interpreted in industry and how to avoid this issue on future production runs.

Title: Is subject injectivity necessary for cross-issuer person-uniqueness in nullifier-based deduplication?

Vozda et al. "Proof-of-Uniqueness ..." available as ePrint 2026/1725 (PDF) assumes subject injectivity — one person maps to one identifier within a coordinated issuance namespace — as a precondition for nullifier-based deduplication, and note that context-scoped tags cannot deduplicate across contexts. Deployed systems (CanDID, World ID, SyRA) appear to satisfy this by construction rather than by relaxing it.

Is the injectivity precondition known to be necessary, or only sufficient? Specifically: is there a result showing that person-level uniqueness across issuers with mutually independent identifier namespaces is impossible, or has the multi-authority anonymous credential line of work approached this from another direction?

Update: the same requirement appears in multi-authority attribute-based encryption, where Chase (2007) and Lewko and Waters (2011) rely on a global identifier to tie attributes from independent authorities to one user. That is collusion resistance rather than deduplication, but the constraint looks identical: independent authorities need a shared anchor. I have not found this stated as a general result anywhere.

Title: Geofencing area spans two UTM zones

I'm, working on a geofencing project where I need to geofence, that is, track real time position of cattle, determine whether is inside or outside the fence and calculate distance to the perimeter. The fence is defined with a polygon created with a set of GPS coordinates (lat, lon) given by the user.

To do all the logic/mathematic involved, I think it's better to convert the spheric GPS WGS84 coordinates into rectangular (metric) coordinates, since everything is easier to compute with classic Euclidean geometry, and since I think areas are short enough to neglect Earth's curvature. We are talking of a parcel that at most is 1km x 1km.

I was searching for implementations to implement in an embedded MCU and I found a lot of development for UTM projections. I understand that the easting coordinate is relative to the central meridian of the zone. Since there isn't an absolute easting and since I need to be prepared to every possible case, what happens if one of the border lines (between two zones) crosses one of my client parcels? It's acceptable to "extend" a zone a few kilometers if I fall in this situation? How much inaccuracy could result from this? Which other alternatives should I consider?

Title: How quickly can a unique language develop?

My setting has a space colony which is settled by mixed groups of colonists who originate from multiple countries and speak several different languages. Although it enjoys an early surge of immigrants it is quickly discovered that there are unforeseen external factors that make living on this colony much more hazardous than originally expected. As news of this spreads immigration ceases and eventually nearly all contact is lost with the colony.

Fast forward about 300 years and contact is reestablished, however it is discovered that the descendants of the settlers now speak a completely unique language with little resemblance to any of original languages spoken there. By little resemblance I mean that a native speaker of any of the old languages could listen to a full conversation spoken in the new language and be unable to identify more than one or two random words. Is that a realistic timeframe for a unique language to develop? And if not then how long would it take?

I did review this question: How to make a language evolve quickly?

However, that specifically asks how to force a language to change and gives no set time limit. For my setting the new language needs to develop naturally and preferably within the period of two to three hundred years.

Title: Why "seven o'clock" but not "king o'hill"?

This is actually a phonological question.

Merriam Webster's etymology entry for o'clock explains that it is a

contraction of of the clock

But, if we look at a structurally similar expression such as king of the Hill, the construction appears to be the same. Why, then, did it not contract into something like king o'hill? In other words, why is the reduction found in o'clock not a general or productive process? Is there something special about o'clock that allowed this particular contraction to become lexicalized while other seemingly parallel expressions did not?

Title: How do those who agree with Emanuel Swedenborg's teachings explain Romans 10?

Emanuel Swedenborg strongly rejected the doctrine of salvation by faith alone. He considered it one of the major theological errors in Western Nicene Christianity.

After spending nine chapters explaining the role of faith, Paul gives the declaration of faith which results in salvation.

5 For Moses writes about the righteousness that is based on the law, that the person who does the commandments shall live by them. 6 But the righteousness based on faith says, "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?'" (that is, to bring Christ down) 7 "or 'Who will descend into the abyss?'" (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). 8 But what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart" (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim); 9 because, if you confess with your mouth Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. 10 For with the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved. 11 For the Scripture says, "Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame." 12 For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, bestowing his riches on all who call on him. 13 For "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." (Romans 10)

Salvation is from faith to faith (Romans 1:17). Old Testament faith, all who call upon the name of the Lord will be saved (Joel 2:32; cited by Peter Acts 2:21) to New Testament faith: God raised Jesus from the dead. Romans was written around 56 AD, long before Nicene and "Western Christianity." It is considered the most comprehensive explanation of the Gospel upon which the Church was based.

How do those who agree with Emanuel Swedenborg's teachings explain Romans 10?

Title: Should I accept a PhD program offer at a much lower ranked university if it feels like a better fit?

I’m in the lucky position to have 2 PhD offers and I understand this is a subjective choice but was hoping to receive guidance and advice about which to pursue for the best prospects post-PhD. For context this is in engineering and both opportunities are in the UK.

Option A is at a top 10 global university with a research group that broadly aligns with my interests but in a domain I have no experience and I’m not sure I could call my passion. Additionally the project is partnered with defence which the supervisor has admitted could lead to issues with publishing due to secrecy restrictions. My other worry is that while the supervisor has been eager and helpful I’ve struggled to get a hold of him, very consistently having to send multiple messages over multiple weeks to get a response and am worried that that could continue during the PhD.

Option B is at a low tier (around 500th in the world) university. However the research group is very well funded and considered the top research lab in the UK in their specific sub-domain. The supervisors have been very eager, supportive and accessible throughout the application process. My main concern is that the sub-domain the lab works in is fairly niche and outside of it I worry that a PhD from university B will carry little weight. This to me is an issue as the work I would be doing is not necessarily restricted to the sub-domain and is more about designing systems to apply the work the lab is famous for. Meaning I would potentially be looking at postdocs/jobs in a separate field in which the university offers little to no name recognition.

I want to accept option B but am worried about the consequences of having PhD from a low tier university on my prospects post-PhD and so am looking for any advice.

Title: Has any game before Morrowind had more than its 17 unique equipment slots?

Morrowind has 17 slots for equipment that aren't interchangeable and can be used together. Rings don't count because it doesn't matter which hand they're on, so I only count them once.

The slots I count, therefore, are:

The clothing:

1. Shirt,
2. Pants,
3. Belt,
4. Skirt,
5. Robe
6. Amulet,
7. Ring

Armour-only slots are:

8. Cuirass/Chest Plate,
9. Helmet,
10. Greaves,
11. Left Pauldron,
12. Right Pauldron,
13. Shield.

Slots that you can equip either clothing OR armour in are:

14. Boots or Shoes,
15. Left Glove or Left Gauntlet/Bracer,
16. Right Glove of Right Gauntlet/Bracer.

- Weapon because it seems they could be enchanted with a Constant Effect of something that's useless in combat, like Light or Soul Trap, so I'll count them as equipment instead of just weaponry.

Has there been a game before Morrowind's release in 1 May 2002, that had more than 17 equipment slots? And if multiple such games do so, the tiebreaker will be who had more, and then who had more, earlier.

Title: Could Edwardian engineers have built a spacecraft to reach earth orbit?

Konstantin Tsiolkovsky published the rocket equation in 1903, but it was relatively unknown even within the Russian Empire in our time line.

Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation: $$\Delta v = v_e \ln \frac{m_0}{m_f}$$

However, for our purposes, the rocket equation is noticed and republished across Europe and America, sparking a great deal of interest and experimentation. Rockets have been well known in Europe and many other parts of the world, but until the publication of the Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation, there was no empirical method to calculate or optimize performance. Now it is possible to make calculations to develop much longer range and more powerful rockets than the small and short ranged artillery and signal rockets available before.

Given the competitive urge to build the "largest" or "most powerful" objects and devices among engineers of the day, it would soon be apparent that the rocket equation could provide the calculations for the basis of a rocket which could reach space or even go into orbit around the Earth.

Although there may have been a desire to build such a rocket, would it actually have been possible given the state of the art of Victorian/ Edwardian era science and technology?

Title: The Meeting At The Table

This story is completely ficticious. I wrote it.
I have used a mixed format, script-like and story-like, only because I thought it would be easier to identify the speakers.

The Meeting At The Table

They came together in a smoke-filled room, thrust together for the latest phase of an ongoing concern. Each of the four took their place quietly and orderly, dressed to the nines. The old man, it came as no surprise, was first to speak.

OLD MAN (OM): Where's the other one?

The two young men sitting on either side stiffened at the officious tone, but the old woman, seated opposite, took no notice.

OLD WOMAN (OW): They'll be here. If my guess is right, this one has an issue with taking things seriously.

OM: Yes. That's what happens when you don't have to work to come out on top. To the business at hand: obviously, I should take the lead when it starts. I am the--

OW: You're most likely to offend them with your aggression. Wouldn't surprise me one bit if you knocked one of them on the head. Perhaps it would be better if I start. I am the most empathetic among us, I'm sure you'll all agree?

After the briefest respectful pause, one of the young men, fondling a ring on his finger, spoke.

YOUNG MAN 1 (YM1): Forgive me, but all the tenderness in the world won't secure a victory for our side. As I've been the most successful of our set, it's only logical that I should begin the--

At this point, the other young man, sitting opposite and fiddling with the patch on his eye, interrupted.

YOUNG MAN 2 (YM2): Only if success is measured strictly in pecuniary terms. I am the one who gets things done. I do the work while you lot pursue your wars, your sentiments, your wealth. I'll go first in this pha--

YM1: Yes, the world absolutely needs ditch diggers like you. However, my talents are--

OM: It's about time! You're late, though I'm not surprised.

This interruption was addressed to a fancy man who slid quietly into the group, a casual smile on his face. Sitting, he waved his hand with a nonchalance that irritated the old man, as one might expect.

FANCY MAN: Better late than never, is what I like to say. And, to look at all of your dour, sour faces--I have to ask: when's the funeral?! Never mind, I am at your disposal. And you're lucky to have me, you all know I always win. And, no! You boys can make fanciful claims all you like, but neither of you is as effective as I.

The fancy man chuckled with some delight, oblivious to the tension in the group.

YM2: May I be practical, as ever, and suggest that we get on with the matter of selecting our order of presentation?

At this point, the group received one very important piece of information. The correct plan became clear in short order, and it succeeded. It would be some time before all in this group would meet again.

What is actually going on in this scene? Identify the players.

Title: Why no prayers on Yom Kippur for an easy death?

The Yom Kippur liturgy speaks about who will live and who will die, as well as about having a full or truncated lifespan. Also, we ask for a long, good life.

But why is there no prayer for the manner of one's death, for example, that if one is destined to die, it should be a peaceful or painless death?

Certainly, people in earlier generations were well aware of the suffering associated with some forms of death, as well as the possibility of dying peacefully in one's sleep.

Is there a theological or halachic reason that the Yom Kippur liturgy focuses on the length of one's life but does not ask for an easy or peaceful death?

Related: Is there a prayer "for an easy death"?

Title: Extracting a first order proof from a non first order proof

Not a logician so apologies in advance if I don't state things perfectly. (Also in advance: I am not giving more specifics unless they are on the order of "How many quantifiers are you using." Also, and this should go without saying, I only want to hear from actual people, not people who are trawling [this site] for questions to answer with money for clout.)

I have a finite list of axioms A in a first order language L and an L-sentence s (really a family of sentences) so that every model of A is a model of s. The proof I have of this latter fact is very non first order - Zorn's lemma to find maximal subsets with some nice property, compactness to prove things about subsets relative to those maximal nice subsets, quantifying over N, etc. This proof implies models of A have some property that makes s completely obvious. Of course completeness tells me there is a first order proof of s from A. The non first orderness is pretty ordinary mathematics.

Are there techniques for "extracting" first order proofs from non first order proofs in a scenario like this? I don't really care if they are ginormous, as long as I can understand how they are constructed.

Title: What on earth is a “laconic drawl”?

A person is ‘laconic’ if they use very few words, especially with the confrontational terseness of of unintimidated Spartans. A way of speaking counts as a ‘drawl’ if it is slow and elongated, especially when it comes to vowels. Clearly these words are pointing in different directions: one naturally thinks of a laconic speaker as employing clipped syllables, not wasting their breath on the enemy.

And yet “laconic drawl” appears to be a collocation: I found 72 results in Google Scholar, presumably in edited writing. One might conclude that the writers are deliberately trading in paradox. Maybe they’re talking about an amusing case in which a laconic speaker takes a few words and drawlingly stretches them out to the length of a normal sentence. But the examples don’t seem to fit:

- Biting into one of the 12-year-old biscuits, KerryJayne announced in her laconic drawl, “Poor John Darby, they gave the bastard stale biscuits.” [This doesn’t seem laconic at all.]
- Mr Robin Ramsay's face, now deadpan as a comedian's, now mobile and droll; his voice, with a hundred subtle modulations of its laconic drawl, were alike perfect... [This doesn’t seem to have anything to do with laconic speech.]
- Famous for his slow, laconic drawl he was quick to take on the mantle of Territory jingoism. [Here we get whiplash, as we go from ‘slow’ to ‘laconic’ and back to ‘drawl’.]
- When Snoop half-sings, in his laconic drawl, the mantra “I don’t love them hoes,” the tonal semantics do not overtly suggest a testy disavowal or fear of female sexuality. [Five may be a small number of words, but there’s obviously nothing the slightest bit laconic about Snoop Dogg’s rapping.]

Can anyone explain what’s going on here? Thanks!

EDIT: I think I’m being asked to consult a dictionary. I’ll use the OED and Merriam-Webster:

laconic (OED): 1.a. (With capital initial.) Of or pertaining to Laconia or its inhabitants, made or written in Laconia; Lacedæmonian, Spartan. Now rare. 1.b. Characteristic of the Laconians; Spartan-like. 2. Following the Laconian manner, esp. in speech and writing; brief, concise, sententious. Of persons: Affecting a brief style of speech.

laconic (M-W): using or involving the use of a minimum of words: concise to the point of seeming rude or mysterious

drawl (OED): 1. The action or an act of drawling; esp. a way of speaking slowly using prolonged vowel sounds. Now often associated with accents of the American South. 2. Slow loitering pace. rare.

drawl (M-W): a drawling manner of speaking [based on the following verb meanings: (intr.) to speak slowly with vowels greatly prolonged, (tr.) to utter in a slow lengthened tone

I think it’s clear that these dictionary entries do not resolve the question, but rather make the question more pressing.

Title: Why is it so that even in the succeding theory of physics to Newtonians mechanics, the conceptual scaffolding of the theory still transfers?

In particular let us restrict to the successions of Newtonian mechanics by Quantum Mechanics and General relativity, each independently. I find it curious that many of the basic notions that comes up in the conceptual scaffolding of the theory of Newtonian Mechanics also transfers, at least in name, to these other succeeding theories.

In particular concepts such as position, momentum, energy and so on. Somehow there seems to be something in how Newtonian Mechanics was built up, even if the whole thing is a "limiting case". It is even more curious when we consider the fact that these succeeding theories disagree on fundamental aspects of reality. E.g time in relativity vs QM.

Could it be explained what is the "core" of the Newtonian chapter of understanding physics that we can take away for a general understanding of the theories of physics? And further why this would be justified to be the core.

Title: How to renew Linux /etc/machine-id on a runnning system?

The situation: two or more cloned Ubuntu 24.04.4 VMs already in production share the same /etc/machine-id. There is also /var/lib/dbus/machine-id but it is just a symbolic link to /etc/machine-id so I presume nothing needs to be done about it.

I've searched various instructions on how to fix this. Some suggestions don't seem to work at all, mentioning these so that no one suggests these as the solutions:

Remove the file /etc/machine-id and reboot the machine, a new fresh machine-id will be created on reboot:

No it won't.

Remove the file /etc/machine-id and run "sudo systemd-machine-id-setup":

This just regenerates the old machine-id, not a new one.

The procedure that seems to do what I want is:

sudo rm -f /etc/machine-id
sudo dbus-uuidgen --ensure=/etc/machine-id
sudo dbus-uuidgen --ensure

After this there is a fresh new machine-id and the symbolic link /var/lib/dbus/machine-id also seems to still work. However, the dbus-uuidgen manual page states:

The important properties of the machine UUID are that 1) it remains unchanged until the next reboot and 2) it is different for any two running instances of the OS kernel.

So does that mean I shouldn't at any cost regenerate a new machine-id while the system runs, and if so, how should I generate a new one? Is it possible at all without a reboot, without causing big problems?

Title: Preparation of Methyl Orange Indicator Solution from Powder

I've recently run out of methyl orange indicator solution in the small lab where I work.

Fortunately, there was an old jar of methyl orange powder tucked away in a cabinet; unfortunately there is no documentation in the lab spelling out the preferred way to make-up the standard solution from scratch. (And the old solution's handwritten label saying only "methyl orange" didn't offer any more information to work from.)

Luckily, it is a common indicator, and plenty of online sites can be found selling 0.05% w/v aqueous solutions (or 0.1%, 0.04% etc.) and additional google searches mention potentially using ethanol instead. So it seems like there is a fairly wide spectrum of possibilities here, and it should hopefully be a bit forgiving. As we had plenty of old indicator powder on-hand, I attempted to make-up a 0.05% w/v aqueous solution.

$$ 1\% \ (w/v) = 1g \ / \ 100mL \ \ \rightarrow \ \ 0.05\%\ \ (w/v) = 0.5g \ / \ 1000mL $$

The math is simple, weighing out a small amount of powder is simple, adding that powder to a volumetric flask is simple, filling to the mark with DI water is simple. So, here we go!

And...It didn't turn out the same as what I had been previously working with. I created a cloudy solution with a ruby color - compared to the clear solution with a neon-orange color I was familiar with. (Also, the cloudiness has a kind of glittery quality to it as you swirl it, like you sometimes see in some soaps/lotions.) It has now been ~24h and the solution does not seem to have changed from what I started with.

So, what went "wrong" and how can I troubleshoot it?

Is this just how methyl orange acts in pure DIW and I should have used pure ethanol instead? (For what it is worth, a few drops of the cloudy solution still seems to work properly for the qualitative colorimetric tests we have been doing.)

Do I need to give it more time or warm the solution in a hot water bath? (i.e. Is this just a poor/slow solubility issue?)

Is this some sort of pH issue and a few drops of NaOH or HCl or something is all that is needed to clear the solution up?

UPDATE

Thanks to everyone for their helpful suggestions and answers.

The specific powdered Methyl Orange solids I was working with were in fact the sodium salt form of the molecule (CAS: 547-58-0) and not the acid form (CAS: 502-02-3).

For more general troubleshooting data, I had run a rough pH test (old probe, calibrated a day or so previously) on the cloudy red sample and found a pH ~3.2 which makes sense as that is toward the red end of Methyl Orange's transition window of (red) 3.1 - 4.4 (yellow).

Following the suggestions of heating/warming the solution I placed the volumetric flask full of the cloudy solution into a hot-water bath and left it there for a bit. When I returned the cloudiness was gone and I had a crystal-clear ruby-red solution! (And not even a speck of undissolved solids or precipitate in the bottom of the flask.) Apologies to anyone looking for more data/specifics, but I measured neither temperature nor timeframe for this; suffice to say the temperature was below water-boiling and the timeframe was relatively short (definitely less than an hour by the time I came back to check on it).

I then used a couple drops of the indicator in an acid-base titration test on a known sample using the usual methods here in the lab and found the indicator solution worked as expected. (Not surprising as even the cloudy solution worked as-expected, despite not looking as-expected.)

Following this I saved some (~5%) of the solution in a glass dropper for lab use as originally intended.

To another small sample I added a few drops of sodium hydroxide solution until reaching pH ~7; at this concentration and pH the sample now better matched the orange coloration I remember the indicator solution having. (And yes, it still worked as-expected when running a titration.)

The remainder (~900mL?) was added to a clean HDPE bottle for storage. Returning the next day, after the sample had plenty of time to cool, I found that a precipitate had formed in the bottom of the bottle. I am not about to invest the time and effort of filtering, drying, and weighing the precipitate in an attempt to quantify the amount precisely; however, by eye, the volume of precipitate seems to be roughly half the original dry powder in a weighboat (possibly aligning with the 2g/L reference highlighted by DrMoishePippik).

For the near-future I believe I'll leave the solution as-is with the precipitate in the bottom - though I may ultimately decide to take of the supernatant and discard the precipitate.

Again, thanks for all the help and discussion!

Title: Preservation of norm of electron spin under Lorentz transformation

The spin state of an electron in the rest frame (Morse and Feshbah page 101) is described as $$s=a_1 e_1+a_2 e_2$$ where $e_1$ and $e_2$ are unit vectors of two opposite spin directions and are complex. Similarly

$$s^*=a_1^* e_1^* +a_2^* e_2^*$$

In the coordinate system moving in the $\bf x$ direction with speed $u$, the unit vectors transform as

$$e_1^{+}=\alpha _{11} e_1+\alpha _{12} e_2$$

$$e_2^{+}=\alpha _{21} e_1+\alpha _{22} e_2$$

$$e_1^{*+}=\alpha _{11}^{*} e_1^{*} + \alpha _{12}^{*} e_2^{*}$$

$$e_2^{*+}=\alpha_{21}^{*} e_1^{*} + \alpha_{22}^{*}e_2^{*}$$

$$\alpha_{11} = e^{\alpha/2},$$ $$\alpha_{22}=e^{-\alpha/2}$$

and

$$\alpha _{12}=0,$$ $$\alpha _{21}=0$$

However $\alpha$ is defined by

$$\tanh(\alpha) =u/c$$

Now for the norm of $s$ to be preserved $\alpha$ cannot be real. How can it be complex ?

Title: How to Define a Menu in Geometry Nodes

Switch nodes (Switch, Menu Switch, Index Switch) all support the Menu data type/input type. However, it is not possible to plug a menu from the group input into them, for this way they won't be defined; also doing this leads to this error message: "Use node groups to reuse the same menu multiple times" even if the menu is only used in one occasion.

So the real question is How to define menus that can be fed into the inputs of switch nodes that have their data type/input type set to menu, and how to later select items from those menus through the modifier interface?

Title: In what sense is the Holy Spirit said to be completing the works of salvation?

The New Testament presents salvation as being accomplished through the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ. For example, Jesus says, “It is finished” (John 19:30), and Hebrews speaks of Christ having offered one sacrifice for sins.

At the same time, the New Testament attributes an ongoing work of salvation to the Holy Spirit. The Spirit regenerates believers (Titus 3:5), sanctifies them (2 Thessalonians 2:13; 1 Peter 1:2), seals them for the day of redemption (Ephesians 4:30), and ultimately gives them life and resurrection (Romans 8:11).

Therefore:

In what sense can the Holy Spirit be said to complete or bring to completion the work of salvation accomplished by Christ?

Is the distinction that Christ accomplished salvation objectively through His death and resurrection, while the Holy Spirit applies that salvation subjectively to individual believers through regeneration, sanctification, and resurrection?

If so, how should passages such as Philippians 1:6 (“he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion”) and Romans 8:13–23 be understood in relation to Christ's declaration that “It is finished”?

Title: Is rim tape fundamentally necessary, or merely advisable?

The other day I was part of a conversation about various causes of flat tires, one being a spoke itself puncturing the tube.

I am trying to understand better if this is a failure mode inherent to the design of bicycle wheels, or just an occasional misfortune.

The common design of spokes I have seen have one end in a curve, terminating in a wider head you slot through a hole in the hub.

The other end is threaded, and you screw it into the spoke nipple.

Without rim tape, I guess we can imagine that as long as the spokes are of a correct length, they will not go further than the nipple and jut outwards from the wheel.

My current understanding of the standard pneumatic tire design is that the inner tube provides the pressure, and the tire provides the tread, protection for the inner tube, and inward force holding the inflated tube in place.

A lot of the preventative measures for avoiding flat tires amount to protecting that inner tube from anything that could puncture it.

Is rim tape there just in case something goes wrong, like a spoke nipple breaks or gets stripped, and a spoke suddenly spears through; or is it more fundamental, like the surface of the wheel is uneven due to all the holes for the spoke nipples, so it's much better to give it an even surface for the pressurized inner tube to press against? Some told me a pressurized inner tube can "prolapse" into one of those holes / dips where the spoke nipples are.

I think what bears on the question is how strong your rim tape should therefore be - electrical tape might cover those little dips / ruts where the spoke nipples are, but it might not prevent a broken spoke from spearing through.

Related

- If a tubeless-ready rim has no tire-facing holes other than the valve hole, is rim tape still necessary?

Title: Can a database be subject to multiple Managed Instance links?

This documentation says a couple of things that suggest that you can replicate the same database multiple times through Managed Instance link. It says

"you can [...] replicate the same database to multiple SQL managed instances, by configuring multiple links - one link for each database to managed instance pair."

and

"A single SQL Server instance can create multiple parallel database synchronization links with several SQL managed instances, even in different Azure regions, with a one-to-one relationship between a database and a managed instance."

So, suppose that you have exactly one database on-prem and that you use Managed Instance link to replicate it to Azure. Then:

- Can you use Managed Instance link again to replicate exactly one already-MI-linked on-prem database to another Azure Managed Instance in another Azure region?
- If so, how?

- Is it required to daisy chain like a distributed availability group? That is, would you be forced to MI link from on-prem to MI, then MI link from that MI to another MI in another region?
- Or can you just do it directly from the on-prem SQL Server instance? That is, can one database on one on-prem SQL Server instance support two MI links to two different Managed Instances in two different Azure regions?

Title: How does a burlap sack interact with Spirit Guardians?

The Villains Clarence and Bailey are looking to kidnap Nathan from his castle for nefarious reasons. Bailey has put Nathan in a burlap sack, and is carrying him out when the The Villains are spotted by the guards. Clarence, being a cleric, casts Spirits Guardians (Player's Handbook p. 278):

When you cast this spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by it. An affected creature's speed is halved in the area, [...]

Clarence designated Bailey as an unaffected creature, and wishes to also target Nathan, but he is inside the bag. This raises some questions and follow up questions, based on the answer to the previous:

-

Can Nathan be chosen by Clarence as an unaffected creature? By the spells description, I would assume not, as the sack completely encases Nathan. But a burlap sack would make it clear that Nathan is inside the sack, and may even be closer to a piece of cloth armor than total cover.

-

If in the first scenario Nathan cannot be designated unaffected, when his turn in initiative begins he is inside the radius of the Spirit Guardians spell. Is he damaged by the attack? Or does the total cover provided by the burlap sack from line of sight also provide total cover from the spell? Or does the fact he is being carried by Bailey count him as a carried object, and by designating Bailey as unaffected, Nathan is also unaffected?

-

On Bailey's turn, she drops the bag to make an attack with her two handed great sword, and does not pick it back up this round.

-

a. If Bailey's carrying of the bag made Nathan unaffected by the spell: when Nathan's turn comes back around, will he now be vulnerable to the spell? Or would previously designating Bailey as unaffected apply to the creature in a sack she was carrying as long as this casting is active?

-

b. If the sack is providing total cover to Nathan: after Nathan and his sack are dropped, he attempts to crawl out of the range of the spell before opening it and fleeing from The Villains. Does the spell's halved movement affect Nathan? As a DM, I would treat Nathan as Prone and walking through Difficult terrain while inside the sack, so his 30 ft movement speed is reduced to 10ft, and if the Spirit Guardians applies, it would be further Halved to 5ft.

state:
Title: Can a Hamiltonian commuting with a sector-label operator generate transitions between its sectors?

Suppose a Hilbert space has a direct-sum decomposition

$$ \mathcal H=\bigoplus_{n\ge 0}\mathcal H_n, $$

where the sectors are eigenspaces of a self-adjoint operator $\hat S_c$,

$$ \hat S_c|\psi_n\rangle=s_n|\psi_n\rangle. $$

Let $\hat J$ be a self-adjoint generator of unitary evolution,

$$ U(\tau)=e^{-i\hat J\tau}, $$

and suppose

$$ [\hat J,\hat S_c]=0. $$

A separate clock/phase operator $\hat S_t$ is introduced with the intended canonical relation

$$ [\hat J,\hat S_t]=i\kappa. $$

My question is:

Can $\hat J$, while commuting with $\hat S_c$, generate genuine transitions

$$ \mathcal H_n\longrightarrow\mathcal H_m,\qquad m\neq n, $$

or must $U(\tau)$ preserve every eigenspace of $\hat S_c$?

If the latter, what is the standard operator structure for introducing genuine sector-changing evolution while retaining a separate clock/phase operator? For example, would one require ladder/shift operators that do not commute with $\hat S_c$?

I am particularly interested in the spectral/operator-algebraic issue rather than in a specific physical model.

Title: What causes an undetectability bug in BfME II/RotWK and how do I prevent it from happening?

There's a serious bug in Battle for Middle-earth II/Rise of the Witch-king's (including vanilla only) skirmishes where remaining opponents eventually stop sending their armies at you because you become invisible to them, unless you cross a specific radius from their fortress. The opponent makes siege units for instance, but doesn't send them to you, because it cannot detect you for some reason. This bug happened both in a CD version I played long ago (on Windows 7), and in a current version of BfME II/RotWK I have. The bug didn't appear right away (during the first skirmishes); the buggy behavior only began to appear later eventually. During the skirmish it isn't present right away either, but begins only after some time or after you defeated some of the opponents.

SITE A:

- Network: 192.168.1.X

SITE B:

- Public IP: 10.20.30.40
- Network: 172.18.0.X

We have a HikVision NVR at SITE B which has 2 cameras connected directly to the NVR. The NVR has a "Virtual Host" option that allows access to cameras connected directly to the NVR using a url with the NVR IP address and ports from 65001 and upwards such as: http://172.18.0.10:65001/ These virtual host URL's work locally at SITE B but do not work from SITE A over the VPN tunnel, the URL just times out.

Can anyone suggest why this is not working and how to fix or diagnose further?

From SITE A we CAN access the following things no problem over the VPN:

- DrayTek web interface on 172.18.0.254

We have not set up or enabled/disabled any firewall or rules, but can't understand why most ports work (like 8000) but the Virtual Host ports (like 65001) don't work.

Title: What parts of speech can take the three types of interrogative clauses as complements?

Background

While studying interrogative clauses in French, I made some generalizations about the parts of speech that allow an interrogative clause to function as a complement. I found that these parts of speech can be:

- noun
- adjective
- verb

For example, in French:

- noun

Je me pose la question [si je peux payer en dollars].

- adjective

Je ne suis pas certain si je dois porter plainte.

- verb

Je sais si Marie viendra.

And interrogative clauses can be of the type

- a yes-no question
- an alternative question (this or that)
- a wh-question (who, what, where...).

To save time, the examples I have selected here are all of the yes-no question type, where "si" in French corresponds roughly to "whether" in English.

Meanwhile, in French, a declarative clause introduced by "que" (which is roughly equivalent to a declarative clause introduced by "that" in English) can serve as a complement to the following parts of speech: noun

For example:

- noun

l’hypothèse [qu’il y a de l’eau sur Mars]

- adjective

Il est tout à fait normal [que les enfants soient accueillis dès 8 heures].

- prep.

Le bureau se réunit pendant [que les délégués préparent leurs interventions].

- adverb

Le bureau se réunit alors [que les délégués ne sont pas encore arrivés].

- verb

Pierre sait [que Marie est malade].

Note that the prepositional and adverbial categories may involve parts-of-speech revisions compared to traditional grammar, resulting in structures traditionally analyzed as conjunctions being reanalyzed as "preposition/adverb + que".

By comparing the two sets, we can see that not all PoS's that accept a declarative clause introduced by "que" as a complement also accept an interrogative clause as a complement.

This discussion will carry out a parallel comparison in English. Therefore, before posing the corresponding question for English, we first need to identify which PoS's can take a declarative clause introduced by "that" as a complement. In English, a declarative clause introduced by "that" can serve as a complement to the following PoS's:

- noun

the claim [that Bill is insane]

- adjective

I am certain that Paul is dead.

- preposition

Gowda was an accidental prime minister-not even the choice of his own Janata Dal Party-and represented a departure from his predecessors [in that he came from a backward caste community, the son of poor peasant parents].

(Can a declarative clause introduced by "that" function as the complement of a preposition in English?)

- adverb

The case was so heavy that I couldn’t lift it.

(Can a declarative clause introduced by "that" function as the complement of an adverb in English?)

- verb

Olafur believes [that Björk composed Hyperballad].

My question

In English, which PoS's can take the three types of interrogative clauses as complements?

Title: Performing 'correct' statistical analysis on fluorescent intensity data

I have performed experiments where I am looking at how treating a fungus with an antifungal drug alters the binding of antibodies through fluorescent microscopy. I captured 4-6 images per conditions, in biological triplicate reps (and thus my n = 3), and performed single-cell analysis to quantify the fluorescence intensity of each cell. For each rep, cells analysed fall in the thousands.

I’ve provided an example graph to show the sort of data I’m looking at. Here, as drug concentration increases, we get a trend of increased intensity ≈ increased binding. The statistical analysis is where I am struggling.

With only 3 reps (and from the visual distribution of the data) I believe normality assumptions can be thrown out the window so I believe I’ll need to do a non-parametric in some capacity. I also think that the random variation that arises on a cell-cell basis needs to be accounted for; whilst in the plot I’ve shown the means for each biorep, I don't think comparing the means in this case is an appropriate way to analyse the population, given the spread of the data?

I'm working in R for the purpose of this work. The closest I’ve come to what I ‘should’ do is a mixed-effects model, whereby the model would look something like: Intensity ~ drug concentration + (1│cell)

However, I am not sure exactly if this is an appropriate approach in this instance. Questions I have:

i) Am I over-thinking this and I simply need to just do a Kruskal-wallis or similar?

ii) Whilst I’m mostly interested in comparing with control (0 drug), comparing between all is also interesting; how would I approach this for any of the possible options?

iii) Is trying to account for the distribution actually required?

EDIT 22/09/26

I've looked at log of the data, and just providing an example here for those interested. I do think you would argue in this instance that the difference is clear, and whilst I would probably be happy with that I am certain my supervisor would at least want some statistical analysis that may suggest significant statistically speaking.

(For those interested, we have seen a level of biological significance of the changes we are seeing here, so whether it actually matters if there is a 'statistical' significance is probably by-the-by. Nonetheless, big boss likes seeing a p value :/ )

Title: Is there a RESTORE command to match BACKUP SERVER [...] WITH METADATA_ONLY?

The Question

The Create a Transact-SQL snapshot backup documentation ("T-SQL from snapshot") gives this code block.

BACKUP SERVER
TO DISK = 'D:\Temp\db.bkm'
WITH METADATA_ONLY, FORMAT;

This is great, since it lets you backup everything on a server without needing to know the database names. But what is the RESTORE command to match this?

I presumably could somehow find out the database names and iterate through them to run one RESTORE command per database, but I am assuming the existence of an easier way.

What I've Tried

Later in the documentation, we see RESTORE BACKUPSETONLY in an example. I have repeated this example below. I could not find any other mention of RESTORE BACKUPSETONLY anywhere on the internet except for that one example. It appears to otherwise be utterly undocumented. When I tried it, what I got back was so badly corrupt that it threw some error referencing a .cpp file. I presume that I was therefore completely misusing RESTORE BACKUPSETONLY and have no idea how it is supposed to be used.

RESTORE BACKUPSETONLY
FROM DISK = 'D:\Temp\db1.bkm'
WITH METADATA_ONLY;

Title: Six circles in a rectangle: show that two lengths are equal, using pure geometry

The diagram shows a rectangle, six circles, and a red line segment joining the centres of two circles. Wherever things look tangent, they are tangent. (The tangencies imply that there are three pairs of congruent circles.)

Show that the length of the red line segment equals the height of the rectangle, using only pure geometry (no coordinates, no trigonometry, no polynomials).

I asked this question at [another site], expressing preference for pure geometry. Some proofs were given, including mine, but none of them use only pure geometry.

I think a pure geometry proof is doable, especially after another geometry question of mine was finally solved using only pure geometry.

Title: SQL*Loader control file for a 2-column, tab-delimited, line-feed-terminated file

The file that I have to load consists of tab-delimited records with a VARCHAR column of up to 40 characters and an INT column up to 6 digits wide. The records are terminated with new lines (0x0A). I checked and double-checked the delimiters and terminators, in a hex editor, as well as it is in ANSI encoding.

The sample data looks along these lines (spaces inserted for clarity):

abcdefghijklmn \t 123456 LF
oprstuv \t 7890 LF

The columns in the database table are in reverse of the file:

num NUMBER(9,0)
net VARCHAR2(50 CHAR)

Based on https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/26/sutil/oracle-sql-loader-control-file-contents.html#GUID-CA3A5703-2A9D-47F2-9243-E467033594F1 I came up with the following control file:

OPTIONS (SKIP_INDEX_MAINTENANCE=TRUE)
LOAD DATA
INFILE 'raw-table.' "STR '\n'"
BADFILE 'raw-table.bad'
DISCARDFILE 'raw-table.dsc'
INTO TABLE table
TRUNCATE
FIELDS TERMINATED BY "\t"
(
net VARCHAR,
num INTEGER
)

When I run sqlldr it loads zero records, sends all the 50 first records to BAD, and the log looks as follows:

Version 18.3.0.0.0

   Column Name                  Position   Len  Term Encl Datatype

NET                                 FIRST     *           VARCHAR
NUM                                  NEXT     4           INTEGER

Record 1: Rejected - Error on table TABLE, column NET.
Variable length field exceeds maximum length.

Variable length field exceeds maximum length.

What is it telling me about the reason for the failed load? How should I edit the control file to load this data?

EDIT as per Greg's observation:

With INTEGER EXTERNAL for the NUM field, the log now shows different Len and Term columns, but the result is the same:

   Column Name                  Position   Len  Term Encl Datatype
------------------------------ ---------- ----- ---- ---- ---------------------
NET                                 FIRST     *           VARCHAR

value used for ROWS parameter changed from 250 to 240
Record 1: Rejected - Error on table TABLE, column NET.

(with \t in single or double quotes) but this caused

In Photos on macOS, editing a photo flips the UI to dark mode (or as I call it, "mirror mode"). Dark mode anything is basically unusable on my shiny screen, my office has white walls and lots of windows.

I have my system set to light appearance always, and as far as I can tell there are no UI options in Photos to set the edit background color. I'd prefer a neutral gray, but I'd settle for light mode. (The accessibility invert feature doesn't work because it inverts the photo too).

Is there a way to make the Edit screen show up in light mode? Maybe a variable in the defaults system (defaults write com.apple.photos ...)? Or something harder like flipping a bit in one of the NIB files?

Title: Common Sense Beliefs

As someone new to philosophy, I've always wondered how it is that so many different schools of thought exist regarding metaphysics/existence while at the same time every amateur or professional philosopher holds certain common beliefs regarding their own existence (as we all do) i.e. belief in some sort of external world, other minds etc.

My question is whether there has been a common framework that allows us to establish these common sense beliefs given that they are so universally held.

Say we start with the classic starting point in epistemology : the conscious experience we all have in this present moment. What frameworks allow us to go from here to justifiably holding our beliefs in SOME sort of external worlds and other minds. I realize that abduction is the most common line of reasoning from this point onwards (although I've always struggled to see why a simpler/more 'elegant' solution is more justified).

Or does it simply come down to burden of proof?

Title: When and why did poems start being published with attribution in magazines?

The July 2026 issue of The Atlantic has on its cover Julia Ward Howe's "Battle Hymn of the Republic", her name printed neatly right below the title. The Editor's Note includes this (bolding and link mine):

[The poem] was published in our February 1862 issue without her byline, as was then the custom. One of the many reasons we wanted the "Battle Hymn" to represent The Atlantic on the semiquincentennial anniversary of American independence is that it would allow us to print the poem with Howe's byline on our cover for the first time.

The idea of publishing a writer's work without giving them credit is quite odd to me. I was taught to always cite my sources, for one, but also I thought that part of the reason writers submitted work to prestigious magazines was that they would then get the prestige of having their name appear in the text. Thus I find it curious that publishing a poem sans byline "was then the custom".

I can only ever remember poems (or other literary works, such as short stories) appearing in publications with author names attached. Assuming that the Editor's Note isn't lying, when and why did this become common practice? If "prestigious literary magazines" is too broad a category, feel free to restrict to just The Atlantic

Title: Did the serpent tell Adam he was naked, ʿêrōm?

After the woman was brought to Adam, the narrator makes this statement.

24 Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.25 And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed. (Genesis 2)

The event is narrated as husband and wife being together while not wearing clothes. The phrase they shall become one flesh is a euphuism for sexual intercourse (cf. Genesis 4:1) which is typically without clothes. [This question is not about sexual intercourse. It is about being ashamed if someone other than your spouse sees you without clothes.]

Their nakedness is described as עָרוֹם, ʿārôm, which is often used in terms of birth (Job 1:21, Ecclesiastes 5:15, Hosea 2:3) or in response to being dressed as commanded by the LORD (Isaiah 20:2, 3, 4).

Chapter 2 ends by placing two aspects of marriage in apposition: two being one flesh and the both of them being naked, ʿārôm and not ashamed.

After eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, the narrator explains:

7 Then the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves loincloths. 8 And they heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden. 9 But the LORD God called to the man and said to him, "Where are you?" 10 And he said, "I heard the sound of you in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself." 11 He said, "Who told you that you were naked..." (Genesis 3)

After eating, they attempt to clothe themselves, showing their understanding of nakedness is different. It is how we would understand the meaning today.

When the man says he was naked, he uses the word, עֵירֹם, ʿêrōm not עָרוֹם, ʿārôm and he speaks of his nakedness, not their nakedness.

Also it is interesting, both ʿārôm and ʿêrōm are adjectives, not the noun עֶרְוָה, ʿervâ, which is the most frequently used word to describe being naked (as with Noah Genesis 9:23).

According to the LORD God, someone told them they were ʿêrōm and Adam had gone from the state of being ʿārôm and not ashamed to being ʿêrōm and afraid.

Did the serpent tell Adam he was ʿêrōm?

If not, how do we account for using a different adjective and not the noun?

- Rashi, commenting on Genesis

Title: Does “no self” (not Buddhist idea) prove the self does not exist?

Mostly gotten from the Wikipedia page on personal identity:

The "no-self theory" holds that the self cannot be reduced to a bundle because the concept of a self is incompatible with the idea of a bundle. Propositionally, the idea of a bundle implies the notion of bodily or psychological relations that do not in fact exist. James Giles, a principal exponent of this view, argues that the no-self or eliminativist theory and the bundle or reductionist theory agree about the non-existence of a substantive self. The reductionist theory, according to Giles, mistakenly resurrects the idea[k] of the self[56] in terms of various accounts about psychological relations.[l] The no-self theory, on the other hand, "lets the self lie where it has fallen".[57] This is because the no-self theory rejects all theories of the self, even the bundle theory. On Giles' reading, Hume is actually a no-self theorist and it is a mistake to attribute to him a reductionist view like the bundle theory. Hume's assertion that personal identity is a fiction supports this reading, according to Giles.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_identity

The part about how it says that propositionally the concept of a bundle doesn’t apply to body or psychology is something I’m not sure about. I’m also not familiar with the philosopher who posits this view.

Title: Feedback on Peak detector

I'm working on a peak detector for an audio mixer. I started with this circuit as a reference, and I think I've come up with a similar slightly more efficient and versatile design. I would appreciate any feedback on things that could be improved or maybe won't work as intended or misunderstandings in my description of how the circuit works.

Circuit description: D30 and D29 are used to create reference voltages for the window comparator built with CMP8 and CMP7. When the input signal is above or below the reference voltages, CMP8 or CMP7 pull their output low. When the CMP8 / CMP7 output is pulled low, Q4 turns on and charges C8 and turns on D35. When the CMP8 / CMP7 outputs are pulled high again, C8 cannot discharge through Q4's collector so must discharge through the LED and R46 giving a fast attack and slow release. Release time can be modified by changing C8's value.

The comparator I'm using is an LM393 and the zener diodes are 5v zener diodes.

The main benefits here are the configurable release time which I think isn't present in the original circuit, and slightly fewer components.

Title: What is the proper way to shim a water heater?

My electric water heater sits in the basement floor and the location is not completely flat. To stop its rocking, I had to slide shims under it to fill gaps roughly 1/16” to 1/8”. I planned on 3D printing some plastic shims to replace the wood ones but I am wondering if I should make sure the entire bottom is supported.

Should I spray some expanding foam under the unit as well? Am I overthinking this?
